what_it_does: Quantum computers make errors and need error-correction systems to stay reliable; one advanced type of error correction requires producing special pre-prepared quantum states called 'rotation states,' but these states are produced probabilistically — each attempt may fail and must be retried. Because of this unpredictability, a fixed schedule written in advance wastes a lot of time waiting for states that failed to appear, and frequently rewriting the schedule from scratch on a classical computer adds its own overhead. RESCQ is a real-time scheduler that watches how state production is going and immediately redistributes resources from lower-priority to higher-priority operations whenever a failure is detected, without rewriting the whole schedule from scratch. It also decides how often to recheck and potentially reschedule based on how stable or turbulent the quantum system currently is, so it does not waste classical computing cycles on unnecessary rescheduling during calm periods.
